2 completed phase 3 double-blind studies in subjects with ADHD (study 201 and 301)

design.text: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study comparing three fixed doses of NRP104 (30mg, 50mg, or 70mg) vs. placebo, conducted at 64 centers in the U.S.

citations.quote: This was a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study comparing three fixed doses of NRP104 (30mg, 50mg, or 70mg) vs. placebo.
The study was conducted at 64 centers in the U.S.

population.text: Patients between 6 to 12 years of age with a DSM-IV-TR diagnosis of ADHD.

citations.quote: This study enrolled patients between 6 to 12 years of age, with a DSM-IV-TR diagnosis of ADHD.

endpoint.text: Change from baseline of the ADHD Rating Scale (ADHD-RS Version IV) total score at the last post-randomization treatment week (LOCF).

citations.quote: The primary end point was the change from baseline of the ADHD-RS total score at the last post-randomization treatment week (i.e., week 1 through week 4) for the LOCF dataset.
The ITT samples (total N=285) for NRP104 30 mg, 50 mg, 70 mg, and placebo were 69, 71, 73, and 72, respectively.

result.text: All three doses were superior to placebo on change in ADHD-RS total score: placebo-adjusted LS mean -15.58 (30 mg), -17.21 (50 mg), -20.49 (70 mg); each p<0.0001 vs placebo.

design.text: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, three-treatment, three-period, cross-over study in a laboratory classroom setting evaluating NRP104 (30, 50, or 70 mg), Adderall XR, and placebo.

citations.quote: This was a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, three-treatment, three-period, cross-over study. This study was conducted in a laboratory classroom setting to evaluate efficacy and safety of NRP 104 (30 mg, 50 mg or 70 mg) in treatment of ADHD in pediatric population.

population.text: Pediatric patients with ADHD (mean age 9.1 years).

citations.quote: The subjects enrolled were 56% Caucasian, 23% African American; mean age was 9.1 yrs; and had approximately 63% male subjects.

endpoint.text: Average of the SKAMP Deportment Scores (SKAMP-DS) across the treatment assessment day, rated by the investigator.

citations.quote: The primary end  point was the average of SKAMP-DS across the treatment assessment day.
The total number of subjects enrolled in this study was 52; all 52 subjects were randomized to the double-blind treatment from which 50 subjects completed the study. The ITT samples was N=50.

result.text: NRP104 LS mean SKAMP-DS 0.8 vs placebo 1.7 (difference -0.9), p<0.0001.

target_moa.text: Lisdexamfetamine dimesylate is a prodrug of d-amphetamine; after oral administration it is hydrolyzed to active dextroamphetamine, and the intact prodrug is pharmacologically inactive and does not bind the norepinephrine and dopamine reuptake sites.

citations.quote: NRP104 is a pro-drug of d-amphetamine. The active ingredient in NRP104 capsules is lisdexamfetamine dimesylate which lacks stimulant properties and is pharmacologically inactive. When taken orally, the amide linkage is hydrolyzed in the GI tract, releasing active d-amphetamine.
The parent drug, lisdexamfetamine, does not bind to the sites responsible for the reuptake of norepinephrine and dopamine in vitro.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse events (>=5% and twice placebo) were decreased appetite (39% vs 4%), insomnia (19% vs 3%), upper abdominal pain (12% vs 6%), irritability (10% vs 0%), weight decreased (9% vs 1%), and vomiting (9% vs 4%). Ten percent (21/218) of Vyvanse-treated patients discontinued due to adverse events vs 1% (1/72) on placebo.

detail.text: Amphetamines have a high potential for abuse; prolonged administration may lead to drug dependence and should be prescribed/dispensed sparingly. Misuse of amphetamine may cause sudden death and serious cardiovascular adverse events.
